Umar said the Prophet was dearer to him than all but himself; told he must be dearer than his own self, Umar said he now was, and the Prophet approved.
Judging a labourer's illegal intercourse with his employer's wife, the Prophet returned the ransom, gave him a hundred lashes and a year's exile, and had the confessing wife stoned.
The Prophet swore that the tribes of Aslam, Ghifar, Muzaina and Juhaina are better than Tamim, Amir bin Sa'sa'a, Ghatfan and Asad.
Rebuking a Zakat collector who kept presents, the Prophet asked if he would get them sitting at home, and swore thieves of Zakat carry it on their necks at Resurrection.
The Prophet swore that if they knew what he knows, they would weep much and laugh little.
In the shade of the Ka'bah the Prophet kept swearing that the wealthy are the losers, except those who spend their wealth this way and that.
Not saying 'Allah willing', Solomon lay with ninety women hoping for horsemen in Allah's Cause, but one bore a half-formed child; the Prophet swore saying it would have brought them.
When people marvelled at a gift of soft silk, the Prophet swore that Sa'd's handkerchiefs in Paradise are better.
Hind, once wishing the Prophet's family degraded and now honoured, was told she may feed her children from miserly Abu Sufyan's property only what is just and reasonable.
The Prophet asked whether his companions would be pleased to be a quarter, then a third, of the people of Paradise, and swore he hoped they would be half.
When a man thought repeating Surat al-Ikhlas alone was too little, the Prophet swore that it equals one third of the Quran.
The Prophet told people to bow and prostrate properly, swearing that he sees them from behind his back.
To an Ansari woman with her children the Prophet swore three times that they were the most beloved people to him.
Allah forbids swearing by fathers; whoever swears by Al-Lat and Al-Uzza must affirm Allah's oneness; Abu Musa told a man who swore off chicken how the Prophet expiated oaths.
The Prophet threw away the gold ring he wore with its stone inward, swearing never to wear it, and the people threw away their rings too.
Swearing by another religion than Islam makes one as he says; a suicide is punished in Hell by the same means; cursing or calling a believer disbeliever equals killing him.
Allah tested three men of the Children of Israel, sending an angel who came first to the leper as a stranded traveller with no help but Allah's and then his.
The Prophet ordered his companions to help others fulfil their oaths.
Urged on oath by his daughter to come to her dying child, the Prophet wept, saying this is mercy Allah places in hearts, and Allah is merciful to the merciful.
A Muslim who loses three children will not be touched by the Fire except as far as fulfils Allah's oath.
The people of Paradise are every poor, humble person whose oath Allah fulfils, and the people of the Fire every violent, cruel, arrogant person.
Best are the Prophet's generation and the next two; then come people whose witness runs ahead of their oaths, and elders forbade the young to swear by Allah's covenant.
Whoever swears falsely to take a Muslim's property will meet an angry Allah, as verse 3.77 confirms; Al-Ash'ath says it came about his dispute over a well.
Hell will keep asking for more until the Lord puts His Foot over it, and it says 'Enough, enough' by His Power and Honour as its sides draw together.
In Aisha's account of the slander, when the Prophet sought relief from Abdullah bin Ubai, Usaid bin Hudair swore by Allah's eternity to Sa'd bin Ubada they would kill him.
Aisha says verse 2.225 on unintentional oaths concerns phrases like 'No, by Allah' and 'Yes, by Allah', alongside verses excusing mistakes and Moses' plea about what he forgot.
Allah forgives the Prophet's followers the evil their souls whisper as long as they do not act on it or speak it.
Asked on the Day of Nahr about rites done out of order, such as Tawaf before stoning or shaving before slaughter, the Prophet answered each, 'There is no harm'.
Sent back three times to repeat his prayer, a man was taught to perform ablution, face the Qibla, say Takbir, recite, and bow, prostrate and sit until at rest.
At Uhud, Satan's shout made Muslims attack their own rear, killing Hudhaifa's father despite Hudhaifa's cries, and Hudhaifa asked forgiveness for the killers until he died.
Whoever eats or drinks forgetfully while fasting should complete his fast, for Allah fed him.
The Prophet made two prostrations of forgetfulness after rising without sitting and after praying the wrong number of rak'at, prescribing them for anyone unsure how many he prayed.
Moses' first excuse to his companion, 'Call me not to account for what I forget' (18.73), was his forgetfulness.
Whoever slaughtered his Eid sacrifice before the prayer was told to slaughter another, and Al-Bara, whose family had done so for a guest, offered a young milch she-goat.
The biggest sins are joining others in worship with Allah, undutifulness to parents, unlawful killing and the oath Al-Ghamus.
A false oath for a Muslim's property brings Allah's wrath; the Prophet promised mounts he swore to withhold, and Abu Bakr resumed the aid to Mistah he swore to stop.
As Abu Talib was dying, the Prophet asked him to say 'La ilaha illallah', a word by which he could defend him before Allah.
Two phrases light on the tongue, heavy in the balance and beloved to the Gracious are 'Subhan Allahi wa bi-hamdihi' and 'Subhan Allahi-l-Adhim'.
Whoever dies setting up rivals to Allah enters the Fire, the Prophet said, and Abdullah added that whoever dies without doing so enters Paradise.
Having sworn to keep from his wives for a month, the Prophet stayed in an upper room and came down after twenty-nine nights, saying a month can be twenty-nine days.
